title: USMNT Given Major Injury Boost Ahead of Concacaf Nations League Quarterfinals
subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Sophia VeselyOct 21, 2026Mauricio Pochettino will have his pick of strikers. / David Berding/USSF/Getty ImagesThe U.S. men’s national team will have one more striker available in its ranks for next month’s competitive action, as Ricardo Pepi has returned in thrilling fashion from a muscular injury he suffered in September.

Pepi sank to the ground, grimacing in pain, just eight minutes into club side PSV Eindhoven’s clash with Eredivisie foe FC Twente on Sept. 20. Although he was able to gingerly walk off the pitch and later called the injury “just a minor setback,” he was ultimately unfit to report to the USMNT’s September-October international camp and was replaced on the roster by striker Damion Downs.

After a month on the sidelines—missing the USMNT’s four friendlies as well as five club matches, including two Champions League affairs, Pepi returned to the pitch and made sure it was a comeback to remember. He came off the bench at the hour mark of Saturday’s league match against Willem II, and just over 10 minutes later, he had already found the back of the net. On the receiving end of a cross into the box, he flicked a perfect header to the back post to bring the scoreline to 5–0 at Philips Stadion.

The 23-year-old didn’t stop there, though, assisting Kodai Sano’s goal just four minutes later to bring PSV to six unanswered. The game ultimately ended 7–0, PSV’s most dominant win in nearly two years, dating back to a 8–0 victory against Koninklijke HFC in December 2024.

Ricardo Pepi suffered a muscular injury last month. / Dijks Media/MB Media/Getty ImagesPepi’s recovery timeline aligns with the USMNT’s November international camp, which kicks off Nov. 9 and concludes with the Concacaf Nations League quarterfinal tie against Haiti. The first leg is on Nov. 14 in Kingston, Jamaica, and the second leg is on Nov. 17 in Cincinnati.

Already proven he hasn’t missed a beat, the American will likely expect to be called up next week for international duty. If he does receive the call from manager Mauricio Pochettino, it will signify a massive opportunity for the striker to re-establish himself within the pecking order.

When initially named to the September-October roster, he was the only 2026 World Cup forward that manager Mauricio Pochettino included, meaning he would have likely started the majority of the four matches. His abrupt absence, though, made way for teenage sensations Julian Hall and Justin Ellis to stake their claims to the starting lineups. The two had five goals collectively, making Pepi, who hasn’t scored for the USMNT since 2024, a sincere afterthought.

Patrick Agyemang tore his Achilles in the spring. / Mike Egerton/PA Images/Getty ImagesAlthough Pochettino has reinforced his striker ranks with Hall and Ellis, he will be grateful for the return of Pepi, given the long-term injuries some of the other top strikers in his player pool have experienced recently.

Patrick Agyemang devastatingly suffered a serious Achilles tendon injury in April, just weeks before Pochettino named his final World Cup roster. After playing in both of the USMNT’s March friendlies, the Derby County star had seemed likely to earn a tournament spot. Agyemang is “on course” to return to the pitch in November, but not until “after the international break,” according to Derby manager John Eustace.
“It’s important we don’t rush him back,” Eustace told reporters recently. “Just having him training with us at the moment is brilliant. He is with the rehab team, but he is hitting all the markers.”

Haji Wright, who served as the USMNT’s third-string striker this summer, is also not anticipated to return to full strength until after the international break, having suffered a “very serious” quad injury during preseason for Premier League side Coventry City.
“Haji won’t be back until November at best and I don’t want to put pressure on it because it’s an awkward injury,” the club’s manager Frank Lampard told reporters earlier this month.

Although Pochettino will be without Agyemang and Wright, he has seen the return of World Cup star Folarin Balogun. Post-tournament, the 25-year-old was dealing with “a small issue in one of his legs”; however, the striker has already returned to the pitch for club side Monaco, featuring off the bench in the last four Ligue 1 matches. Whether or not he will be back to his best come mid-November, though, remains to be seen.
*Includes players that have been rostered in the last 12 months.
